title: Tokenisation
summary: How traditional financial assets are represented on distributed ledgers, the legal, operational and technological considerations involved, and the supervisory challenges as market structure evolves.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How traditional financial assets are represented on distributed ledgers, the legal, operational and technological considerations involved, and the supervisory challenges as market structure evolves.
Learning Objectives: Analyse tokenised asset and fund structures
Evaluate the legal and operational risks of tokenisation
Syllabus: Tokenising real-world assets: equities, bonds and funds
Smart contracts governing asset behaviour and transfer restrictions
Claimed benefits: efficiency, transparency and liquidity
Legal enforceability, settlement finality and custody risks
Intended Audience: Supervisors and authorisation staff responsible for, or moving into, oversight of virtual asset service providers
Risk, policy, legal and financial crime specialists working on digital finance
Senior managers shaping the authority's approach to crypto-assets and digital finance
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial supervision, authorisation or financial crime work is helpful. No technical background in blockchain or crypto-assets is required.
Core Reading: FSB, High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Crypto-Asset Activities and Markets (2023)
IOSCO, Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets (2023)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
Basel Committee, Prudential Treatment of Cryptoasset Exposures (2022)
